objections.claim: The Eye-local publish ceremony retains a fail-open TOCTOU window. The approach explicitly permits a self-granted `contents:write` Actions token to mutate the bound draft and relies on re-verifying assets/body “immediately before” the Eye flips `draft:false`. Those are separate GitHub API operations with no stated conditional update binding the flip to the verified draft state. A controller/publisher credential or rogue workflow can delete/replace an asset or edit the body after the final verification and before the flip; the Eye then publishes unverified content. The v* ruleset constrains tag refs, not draft-release mutations, and post-publication verification detects the defect only after public exposure. Require platform-enforced exclusive release mutation during the verification-to-flip interval—such as a verified release-mode custody transition that revokes/disables every non-Eye release-capable credential—or another atomic mechanism, plus a regression that mutates the bound numeric release ID after the last pre-flip check and proves publication is refused.
